claims.text: Minor chromium incorporation into boride-based components will improve resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion during hot-dip aluminum plating.
The proposed intervention may be implemented either as chromium alloying/doping or as a chromium-rich surface layer.
Chromium incorporation will produce a chromium-rich interphase at or near the boride surface.
The chromium-rich interphase will form stable aluminum-chromium oxide layers during contact with molten aluminum.
Chromium will react with oxygen and aluminum in the plating environment to form an aluminum-chromium oxide layer.
The resulting aluminum-chromium oxide layer will be continuous and adherent.
The oxide layer will passivate the surface and reduce direct attack of molten aluminum on the boride matrix.
Reduced direct attack on the boride matrix will lower its molten-aluminum corrosion rate.
Chromium-treated samples will exhibit at least a 30% reduction in corrosion rate or weight loss relative to untreated boride samples under identical exposure conditions.
The intervention should remain effective under standard hot-dip aluminum-plating temperatures when chromium is maintained below approximately 2 wt%.
Maintaining chromium below approximately 2 wt% will preserve the integrity of the boride material.
Excessive chromium content or non-uniform chromium distribution may negate the corrosion-resistance benefit.
Extreme temperatures or aggressive environmental conditions may limit the efficacy of the chromium intervention.
No eligible cited evidence directly confirms chromium doping in boride-based systems under molten-aluminum exposure.
